speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) how many applicants were affected by the technical issues associated with the timely issuance of HDB Flat Eligibility letters since its implementation in May 2023; (b) what were the reasons for these issues; and (c) whether the problem has been fully resolved.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: To bring more convenience and help home buyers make more informed decisions, HDB streamlined the flat buying process by integrating the different eligibility assessments into a single application called the HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The HFE letter provides home buyers with upfront and holistic assessments of their eligibility to buy an HDB flat, receive CPF housing grants and take up an HDB housing loan, before they commence their flat buying journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For the May Build-To-Order (BTO) Sales launch, there were system errors and high application volume.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: HDB redeployed more officers to assist home buyers with flat applications that could not be completed successfully online.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Hence, some home buyers experienced longer processing times for their HFE applications.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: HDB is working hard to process the outstanding applications as quickly as possible and we seek home buyers’ patience and understanding.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: In the lead-up to the October 2023 BTO launch, HDB has carried out additional system enhancements to ensure a smoother flat buying process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: We encourage prospective home buyers to apply for the HFE letter early, at least a month before HDB sales exercises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: To facilitate expeditious processing, home buyers should submit the required information and supporting documents for their HFE letter application.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Some questions for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: One, I do not think the question has been answered vis-a-vis how many applications were affected by the technical issues.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I think the Minister of State replied to say there were 50,000 applications, but that does not answer the question.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The second supplementary question deals with the response to a press query by CNA on this matter and it was stated that the issue affecting the HFE matter has been resolved.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Can I confirm that there would be no issues of that nature for the October exercise?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: And with regard to those applications arising from the May 2023 exercise, how many people are still awaiting positive response to their HFE application?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: By "positive response", I mean a response to the HFE application.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In reply to Mr Pritam Singh's supplementary questions, in terms of determining how many people were affected, we do know that applicants experienced longer waiting times.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: But to measure how many people were affected, it is quite difficult to define it.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, we look at it in terms of the number of people who have reached out to HDB for assistance because they could not complete their applications.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, let us look at them in terms of two categories.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Those who have applications for resale flats – those buyers who urgently require HFE applications to be completed in order to do their resale transactions but were not able to do so and have urgent needs, those that have reached out to HDB have been helped.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: As for the May sales launch, to HDB's knowledge, because they have made transitional arrangements requiring only an indication and intention to buy as well as a preliminary HFE check, this transitional arrangement has not resulted in buyers missing out on the May sales launch.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Can I have the third question again, please?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: In the main, my supplementary questions were really framed with regard to the clarification that HDB gave to the public via CNA.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The Senior Minister of State spoke of what it means by a delay.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, I think the gist of my supplementary question is: how many applications went beyond those 21 days?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: That should be a very simple criterion in terms of understanding what problems were faced by HDB because that is what has already occurred.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: There is another deeper query: in terms of moving forward, are we going to see a repetition of this matter or has the problem been fully resolved, as stated by the HDB's press release?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I note the Senior Minister of State's qualification with regard to BTO sales launches and resale exercises.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Can I just confirm, in so far as HFE applications for resale flats are concerned, is there actually no problem and there would be no issue in getting the HFE within 21 days of application?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We are approaching the end of Question Time.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I should add that there is the issue of whether it meets 21 days' service standard, but there is also the impact – whether or not the delay resulted in, for instance, applicant's not being able to take part in the launch.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Orders of the Day.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
